links.note: WAS 145 Ethanol. The activity warms ethanol and adds alkaline KMnO4 drop by drop; the whole answer is about Baeyer's reagent oxidising ethanol to ethanoic acid - organic oxidation, 142.
WAS 145 Ethanol. The three answers are methanal, butanone and ethanal - naming compounds from a parent alkane, 140.
WAS 149 Micelle Formation, a clear mis-tag. Antifreeze C2H6O is ethanol, oxidised by alkaline KMnO4 to ethanoic acid - 142.
WAS 134 Tetravalency of Carbon. The compound is ethanol and the reaction is its dehydration to ethene by conc. H2SO4 - 145.
WAS 142 Oxidation Reactions, but nothing is oxidised. C2H6O heated with conc. H2SO4 gives ethene, and the question asks the acid's role as dehydrating agent - ethanol's dehydration, 145.
WAS 140 Nomenclature, which is unrelated. The item contrasts ionic-compound properties (no conduction in the solid state) with covalent ones, the contrast this chapter draws at 131.
WAS 134 Tetravalency of Carbon. The answer is the word 'covalent' - 131.
WAS 134 Tetravalency of Carbon, which the item contradicts: six outer electrons identify oxygen, not carbon. Filed on 131, where valence-electron counting for electron sharing belongs.
WAS 137 Structural Isomerism, which the item never touches. NH3 is this chapter's standard covalent example - 131.
WAS 134 Tetravalency of Carbon. The answer is diamond, named as an allotrope - 132.
WAS 134 Tetravalency of Carbon. C60 is fullerene, an allotrope - 132.
WAS 134 Tetravalency of Carbon. Graphite as the conducting allotrope - 132.
WAS 134 Tetravalency of Carbon; the answer is the word 'catenation' - 133, its own concept.
WAS 140 Nomenclature. Single bonds mean saturated compounds - 135.
WAS 140 Nomenclature. Double or triple bonds mean unsaturated compounds - 136.
WAS 144 Substitution Reactions. The item only asks that methane is a saturated compound - 135.
WAS 144 Substitution Reactions. The number of hydrogens in methane follows from carbon's four bonds - 134. KEY DEFECT: the marked answer is 6; methane is CH4, so the correct option is 4.
WAS 137 Structural Isomerism; no isomers appear. Hexane's formula C6H14 is a name-to-formula item, 140.
WAS 140 Nomenclature. The item defines structural isomerism in so many words - 137.
WAS 137 Structural Isomerism. The general formula CnH2n+2 of the alkanes is a homologous-series fact, 139.
WAS 137 Structural Isomerism. General formula of the alkene series - 139.
WAS 137 Structural Isomerism. General formula of the alkyne series - 139.
WAS 136 Unsaturated Hydrocarbons. What is asked is the catalyst (Ni or Pd) for adding hydrogen - the addition reaction, 143.
WAS 146 Ethanoic Acid. Converting an ester back to alcohol and the sodium salt is saponification, and the answer says so - 148.
